the hand clock of the process-group test: its setTimeout method only stores the callback and fires on advance(); it waits for nothing (A277)
source text of a child process the test spawns: setImmediate defers the exit by one event-loop turn, it is not a duration and nothing sleeps
source text of a child process the test spawns: a never-firing keepalive (2^30 ms) that holds the child open until the test sends it a signal; the test waits for the exit event, not for the interval

watchdog of the runGroup helper: cleared on close, fires only when the command hangs and then kills its process group and fails the run; a run that ends normally never waits for it. Removal would need an injected clock in the helper and no test depends on the expiry here

manual end-to-end harness around a real claude/codex session (not part of the test suite run by CI): one-second tick of the supervision loop; real sessions cannot run on a fake clock. Removal would need an event source for the ledger change of the session

manual end-to-end harness around a real claude/codex session: supervision tick that races the exit event of the lead process, so a normal exit does not wait for it; the real session cannot run on a fake clock

manual smoke harness against the real claude CLI (not run by CI or by the suite): definition of its sleep helper and the per-step watchdog that kills the process group on expiry; a real session has no fake clock

manual smoke harness against the real claude CLI: waits two real seconds so that the hook message of the next call has a later second-granular timestamp than the question; the product stamps in whole seconds with no clock seam, so this cannot be faked from the harness (lead decides on a seam)
